text:
lucy: Heads up — starting ~11:02 UTC prod-edge (us-west-2) started returning a lot of 502/504s to customers. ALB shows downstream connection resets and a ton of short-lived outbound connections. Looks like NAT/ephemeral port exhaustion on the egress path. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployment v1.4.2 to prod-edge completed at 10:58 UTC (canary -> 100%)

omar: On it. What do logs show for NAT metrics? If ephemeral ports are exhausted we'd see high `AllocatedConnections` and `ConnectionNotAvailable` in CloudWatch for the NAT GW.

lucy: I pulled CloudWatch: NATGW `ActiveConnections` spiked to ~58k per nat-gw IP and then errors. We have one NAT per AZ right now. Also see many nodes with large `TIME_WAIT` counts.

marta: Classic pattern when many short-lived outbound HTTPS requests are made without keepalive. Are model pulls or a background job spiking?

lucy: Yes — model-fetch workers started a batch around 10:50 to warm cache for the rollout. They spawn ~3000 short lived downloads each across the cluster.

omar: Quick triage commands to run on a problematic node: ```bash
# count TIME_WAIT
sudo ss -s
sudo ss -o state time-wait | wc -l
# check ephemeral port range
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
# check nat GW metrics
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name ActiveConnections --namespace AWS/NATGateway --start-time $(date -u -d '5 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --period 60 --statistics Sum
```

omar: Also check ALB target health and envoy upstream logs for `503`/`reset` patterns.

lucy: Ran the commands. TIME_WAITs are ~45k on several nodes, ip_local_port_range is `32768 60999`. NATGW ActiveConnections peaked then we started seeing `ConnectionNotAvailable` in cloudwatch.

marta: So two levers: reduce outbound connection count (prefer keepalive / pooling / shared egress proxy) or increase NAT capacity (more NATs / NAT instances / add more EIPs). Immediate mitigation: throttle model-fetch concurrency and enable persistent connections from fetchers.

ryan: For short-term emergency: 1) spin up an extra NAT gateway in each AZ (adds more ports/EIPs) 2) route a subset of nodes to an alternative NAT (update route table). I can do that now if we want fast relief.

lucy: Please do. Also lowering model-fetch concurrency by 5x now.

ryan: Spawning spare NATGWs and adding route to private route table for node-subnet-a. ETA ~4m. :hammer_and_wrench:

sre-bot: NATGW-creation job started (job id nat-create-881).

marta: Long-term: we should deploy an egress-proxy pool (Envoy) in each AZ to multiplex connections and enable keepalive/persistent HTTP2 where possible. Also consider VPC endpoints for S3/ECR/model-registry so pulls don't traverse NAT. Ticket INF-324 created for egress-proxy rollout and INF-325 for endpoint gating.

omar: Small kernel tweaks can help but won't fix NAT limits: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` / `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30` — only if application owners are okay with it. Better rely on pooling.

lucy: Quick patch applied: model-fetch concurrency down to 600 (from 3000). We're already seeing 50% drop in new outbound flows. ALB 502 rate falling.

ryan: NATGW spares are up and route updated. CloudWatch shows ActiveConnections spread across more NAT IPs now. Error counters dropping.

lucy: Good — 502s trending down to baseline. Keeping the reduced concurrency for the next 30 minutes while we monitor. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

marta: Postmortem items: include default concurrency limits for background batch jobs, ensure model-fetch client uses `requests.Session()` or HTTP/2, and add egress-proxy + VPC endpoints as infra work.

lucy: I'll update the incident doc and tag INF-324/INF-325. Follow-up: can someone own the kernel sysctl recommendation thread with app teams? @omar?

omar: Happy to. I'll coordinate with platform libs and add guidelines to runbooks.

lucy: Closing thread once we've held 30m with normal error rate. Monitoring now. :eyes:
